howDoI.q: How do I make a layer of scenery slide on a screen that does not scroll?
How do I make far things go slower than near things?
How do I make a slide that comes round with no seam?
How do I make clouds drift across the sky?
How do I make a picture change after a time?
How do I keep a door shut until something happens?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Parallax is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish. It is in the Showcase Tricks group, because it shows how a big game makes layers go by at different speeds, the trick that To the Horizon builds on.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door to go on.

Each level is one screen that never scrolls. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Three Speeds
pages.html:
Level 1: Three Speeds

The FAR HILLS CRAWL, THE FENCE RACES sign hangs on the left. Behind Rima three strips of scenery slide to the left: blue and green hills at the back, a little town in the middle, and a white picket fence nearest of all. The hills barely move, the town goes by at a stroll, and the fence is a blur. The screen is a single picture that never scrolls, yet it seems deep.

The A BAND IS A RING OF BLOCKS sign hangs on the right. Watch the town and the fence for a moment: after a while each one is back where it began, and you cannot see the join.

The door on the right is open from the start, but stay a while and watch first.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A band is one row of one block. Open one.map in the map editor. The hills are a row of the same block along row 3, the town along row 4 and the fence along row 5. Every other cell is plain: sky above, lawn below, and the path Rima walks on.
  • That block is a ring of pictures. Open px1.bbl. The hills block is followed by nine more, each a picture of the same hills moved 2 pixels to the left of the one before. Each has a Next block, and the last points back to the first. The engine swaps the block for its next block after its Time, in every cell that uses it at once, so the whole row slides together.
  • Speed is the step over the wait. The hills move 2 pixels every 4 ticks (half a pixel a tick, about 9 a second). The town moves 2 pixels every 2 ticks, and the fence 4 pixels every tick. The ticks are 18.2 to the second. The nearer a band, the faster it goes.
  • The ring comes round with no seam. A band is drawn to repeat every 20 pixels, the width of a block. After 10 steps of 2 pixels, or 5 of 4, the picture is where it started. The fence has uneven gaps between its pickets, because a regular fence moving 4 pixels at a time looks as if it creeps the wrong way.
  • Blocks it costs. A ring takes one block for each of its pictures: 10, 10 and 5. Together with the sky, lawn, signs and hedges, the level uses 78 of the 150 blocks it may have.
  • It never scrolls. In px.gam the scene's four scrolling settings are all off. Hedges at both sides close the room in.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures, on two posts.

pages.head: Level 2: Drifting Clouds
pages.html:
Level 2: Drifting Clouds

The CLOUDS DRIFT AT TWO SPEEDS sign hangs on the left. High up, thin white wisps drift very slowly. A row lower, round clouds go by twice as fast. The hills below still crawl. Far things are slow, near things are quick, and now it is the sky that does it.

The THE DOOR OPENS WHEN THE SUNS FILL sign hangs on the right. Three outlined suns sit in the middle of the sky. About every 5 seconds another one fills with gold. When the third is full, about 16 seconds in, the bars across the door lift. Walk up to it and wait.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Clouds are bands too. In two.map the wisps are a row of one block along row 0 and the clouds along row 1. In px2.bbl each is a ring of pictures like the hills: the wisps move 2 pixels every 8 ticks, the clouds 2 pixels every 4. The cloud is drawn to repeat every 20 pixels, so one drifts through each block's width.
  • The same ring, a different wait. The wisps and the clouds have the same 10 pictures each. Only the Time differs, so a slower band costs no more blocks than a faster one. To slow a band, lengthen its Time; do not make its step smaller.
  • The suns are blocks that turn into blocks. Each sun is a block with a Next block and a Time. The first sun turns from an outline into a gold sun after 100 ticks; the second does the same after 200 and the third after 300. All of the level's timers start when the level does.
  • The barred door. The door at the right is two blocks. Each is solid with bars drawn over it, and turns into the plain door after the same three waits as the suns. A solid block stops Rima; the plain door is not solid and has a link, so the door works when the bars lift.
  • Its own block file. This level's blocks are in px2.bbl, not level 1's. A block set holds at most 150 blocks and each level needs its own rings.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

This is a picture sliding in place, not a world scrolling by:

  • Nothing really scrolls. Rima walks along a screen that never moves, so he does not get anywhere; the door is always in the same place. A game that follows the hero uses the scrolling settings instead, and then the whole picture moves at one speed.
  • A band repeats every 20 pixels. A mountain 60 pixels wide cannot be one picture; it must be drawn so it repeats.
  • A band slides one way, to the left, because each picture is the one before moved left. A band that went the other way needs its own ring made the other way round.
  • It does not follow Rima. Walking left or right does not speed the bands up, slow them down or reverse them. They go at the same speed whether Rima moves or stands still.
  • A band is whole blocks. It slides inside its row, 20 pixels tall and no more, so a tall band is a stack of rings that must all use the same wait to stay level with each other.
  • A ring costs a block for each picture, out of the 150 a level may have. A band that moves 1 pixel at a time needs 20 pictures.
  • The timers count from when the level starts, and every cell of one block changes together. A block cannot start its clock when something happens, such as Rima arriving.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In px1.bbl change the Time of the fence's blocks from 1 to 2. It slows to half.
  • Change the Time of the hills' blocks to 1 and watch them catch up with the town.
  • In px2.bbl change the Time of a sun to 50, so it fills sooner.
  • Redraw the fence with different gaps between the pickets, keeping the picture the same at its two ends.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one, and To the Horizon uses the same blocks with a road in perspective.
